clue.text: Dog in New Jersey, one attached to army HQ

parts.note: a base is an army's headquarters
postal abbreviation for the US state

explanation.surface: A dog in New Jersey is assigned to an army headquarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attached to' just joins the pieces: the state and the one hang on after the headquarters.
explanation.definitionFit: The basenji is a barkless hunting breed from central Africa.

clue.text: Black Aussie truck in Scottish island

parts.note: abbreviation for black, as on pencils
Australian slang for a pickup, a utility vehicle

explanation.surface: A black Australian pickup turns up on a Scottish island.
explanation.definitionFit: Bute is an island in the Firth of Clyde off western Scotland.

clue.text: Become more inclined to visit writer penning tango

indicators.note: penning means shutting in, as in a pen

parts.note: to see someone is to visit them
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: Feeling more inclined to call on an author who writes tangos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inclined' sounds like willing, but here it means sloping, as a hill does.
explanation.definitionFit: To steepen is to grow steeper, a slope becoming more sharply inclined.

clue.text: Rugby fellow going over part of Belgium

indicators.note: going over suggests flipping back on itself, so the letters read backwards

explanation.surface: A rugby player crosses over into part of Belgium.
explanation.walkthrough: RU+MAN reversed gives NAMUR. 'Going over' might be a try being scored; it is the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Namur is a city and province in Wallonia, southern Belgium.

clue.text: Needy girl kept by funky bloke

indicators.note: something kept by another is held within it

parts.note: short for Diana, a stock girl's name

explanation.surface: A poor girl is kept by a trendy man.
explanation.walkthrough: IN and GENT together hold DI. Bloke is British for a man.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigent describes someone poor, in need of the basics of life.

clue.text: Small tree father brought back, inspired by member's support

indicators.note: to be inspired is to be breathed in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a sling supports an injured arm, a limb or member

indicators.note: something brought back returns the way it came, so the letters run backwards

explanation.surface: A small tree that Dad brought home, held up in a sling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' here is a limb, not a club member: an arm in a sling.
explanation.definitionFit: A sapling is a young tree, still slender and small.

clue.text: Foul reportedly observed by police officer and daughter

indicators.note: reportedly means as said by someone, so the sound matters, not the spelling

parts.note: saw means observed, and in a non-rhotic accent it rhymes with the spelling here

explanation.surface: A crime reportedly seen by a police officer and his daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: In standard British speech 'saw' and 'sor' sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Sordid means dirty or squalid, foul in a physical or moral sense.

clue.text: Nut cooking chips at Vigo regularly

indicators.note: cooking turns ingredients into something new, so these letters get remixed
regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: Nuts and chips frying in a Spanish port town.
explanation.walkthrough: Vigo is a port in Galicia, north-west Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: The pistachio is a green-kernelled nut from a tree native to western Asia.

clue.text: Wine a woman briefly describes at last in slanting script

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter is lost

parts.note: It is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and It
a girl's name standing for a woman

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter only

explanation.surface: A woman describes wine in sloping handwriting.
explanation.walkthrough: IT plus ALIC(e) plus S. 'Gin and It' is gin with Italian vermouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Italics are a typeface whose letters lean to the right, a slanted style of type.

clue.text: Misguidedly get near her tropical tree

indicators.note: misguided action goes astray, so these letters land in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Foolishly approaching her tropical tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenheart is a South American hardwood tree, valued for its dense timber in shipbuilding.

clue.text: Month amphibious troops originally introduced Dutch soldiers

parts.note: the RM, the Royal Marines, Britain's amphibious infantry, article included

indicators.note: originally means at the origin, so only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: In a certain month, amphibious troops first brought in Dutch soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: The troops are 'the Marines', so the article comes along with RM; OR (other ranks) is the usual crossword soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Thermidor was the eleventh month of the French Revolutionary calendar, roughly July to August.

clue.text: Soft rock prince found in the Kent area

indicators.note: what is found in something lies inside it

parts.note: Kent is a county in South East England
Prince Hal, Shakespeare's young Henry V

explanation.surface: Some soft rock with a prince discovered in Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soft rock' sounds like a music genre but is geology. Prince Hal is Shakespeare's young Henry V; Kent lies in South East England.
explanation.definitionFit: Shale is a fine-grained sedimentary stone that splits easily into thin layers.

clue.text: Odyssey of pair keeping 1987 car before one race

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it within

parts.note: British number plates from 1987-88 carried the year letter E: an E-reg car

explanation.surface: The epic journey of two drivers nursing an old 1987 car to one more race.
explanation.walkthrough: UK number plates once carried a letter showing the registration year; 1987-88 cars were E-reg.
explanation.definitionFit: An odyssey is a long wandering journey, which is what a peregrination is.

clue.text: Like some senior councillors raving under tree

indicators.note: in a down clue under means placed below, so the piece before it is written second

parts.note: the alder is a tree of damp ground

explanation.surface: Senior councillors ranting beneath a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'under' puts the second piece below the first, so the tree is written first.
explanation.definitionFit: Aldermanic means relating to an alderman, a senior member of a borough or city council.

clue.text: Protractedly taken in about northern form of writing

parts.note: as an adverb, long means for an extended time

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps another

parts.note: to be had is to be fooled or taken in

explanation.surface: Someone long fooled about the North writes it all out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken in' means fooled, not absorbed; 'protractedly' is the adverb long.
explanation.definitionFit: Longhand is ordinary handwriting, as opposed to shorthand or typing.

clue.text: Polish gang set up attractive lure for victims

parts.note: to hone is to sharpen or polish

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means raised, so the word reads upwards

parts.note: a party is a group or gang

explanation.surface: A Polish gang laid a tempting trap for victims.
explanation.walkthrough: HONE then PARTY reversed (YTRAP). The capital P makes Polish look like a nationality.
explanation.definitionFit: A honeytrap is a scheme using a seductive person to entrap someone, a lure.

clue.text: Restrained introduction to history in class

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a caste is a social class

indicators.note: an introduction comes at the start, so only the first letter counts

explanation.surface: A sober, restrained opening to a history lesson in class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Class' reads as a classroom but means social rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaste means modest and self-restrained, especially in style or behaviour.

clue.text: Intractable objections raised principally by old sailors

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means lifted up, so the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: buts are objections, as in no ifs or buts

indicators.note: principally means mainly or first, so the opening letters are taken

explanation.surface: Stubborn protests raised chiefly by veteran sailors.
explanation.walkthrough: BUTS upwards is STUB, then B and O, then RN.
explanation.definitionFit: Stubborn means obstinate and unyielding, hard to manage or deal with.

clue.text: Conclusion: pig, frog and bulldog all do it

definitions.text: pig, frog and bulldog all do it
definitions.meaning: second reading: each of these words finishes with the same letter, split as three words

explanation.surface: Pigs, frogs and bulldogs all reach a conclusion together.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as END IN G: pig, frog and bulldog each finish with G.
explanation.definitionFit: An ending is the close or final part of something, its conclusion.

clue.text: Abandoned Legoland, heading off for the Lifford area

indicators.note: abandoned can mean wild and unrestrained, so the letters run riot
with its heading off a word loses its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone left Legoland and headed off to Lifford.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the first L of LEGOLAND and rearrange the rest. Lifford is a small town in the Republic of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifford is the county town of Donegal, in north-west Ireland.

clue.text: Walker's extremely smart luxury car

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only the outer letters stay

parts.note: a Roller is slang for a Rolls-Royce

explanation.surface: A pedestrian owns a very smart luxury car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Walker's' is 'Walker is'. Roller is British slang for a Rolls-Royce.
explanation.definitionFit: A stroller is someone who walks at a leisurely pace.

clue.text: Young chap carrying goods, a right dawdler!

indicators.note: carrying something means holding it inside

parts.note: a lad is a young man
G is good, so two goods are two Gs

explanation.surface: A delivery boy carrying goods is a slowcoach.
explanation.walkthrough: LAD holds G+G+A+R: LA-GGAR-D.
explanation.definitionFit: A laggard is someone who lags behind, slow and dawdling.

clue.text: Art work little Albert's left in the open air

indicators.note: has left means has gone away, so that part is removed

explanation.surface: A small Albert left an artwork outside.
explanation.walkthrough: Take AL away from AL FRESCO.
explanation.definitionFit: A fresco is a painting done on wet plaster, a mural artwork.

clue.text: Acquisitive individual tucking into my food, a former crooner

indicators.note: tucking into something means going inside it

explanation.surface: A greedy person helping themselves to my dinner, an old crooner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tucking into' suggests eating, which suits the food in the surface, but it signals insertion. Bing Crosby was the crooner.
explanation.definitionFit: Being money-grubbing means greedily set on gaining wealth, i.e. acquisitive.

clue.text: Knowledgeable about getting hold of Rachmaninoff's first prelude

indicators.note: getting hold of something means holding it inside

parts.note: being into a subject means knowing and caring about it

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of the name alone

explanation.surface: An expert on Rachmaninoff takes up his first prelude.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes inside INTO. Rachmaninoff wrote a famous Prelude in C sharp minor, which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is an introduction, the opening passage before the main piece.

clue.text: Carry on adopting Oscar's ruse

indicators.note: adopting something means taking it in

parts.note: to ply a trade is to carry it on

explanation.surface: Keep going with Oscar's trick.
explanation.walkthrough: O goes inside PLY.
explanation.definitionFit: A ploy is a cunning tactic, a manoeuvre to gain an advantage.

clue.text: Retired fellow at home in cattle-raising country

indicators.note: to retire is to draw back, so the letters go backwards

parts.note: Reg is a stock man's name
being in means being at home

explanation.surface: A retired man stays at home in a farming country.
explanation.walkthrough: REG+IN reversed reads NIGER.
explanation.definitionFit: Niger is a West African nation where herding livestock is a major part of the economy.

clue.text: Deficit which can possibly lead to lengthy cold spell?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an amount by which something falls short

definitions.text: which can possibly lead to lengthy cold spell
definitions.meaning: second reading: a brief autumn, using the American word for that season, comes before a long winter

explanation.surface: A budget gap that may bring on a long, chilly patch.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as SHORT FALL: fall is the American word for autumn, and a brief autumn could be followed by a long winter.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortfall is a deficit, an amount by which supply falls below need.

clue.text: Better thus to pen extremely leisurely song

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, as animals in a pen

parts.note: to cap is to outdo or better

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its ends, so only the outer pair stays

explanation.surface: Better that way to write a really relaxed song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pen' looks like writing; it means enclose. To cap a story is to better it.
explanation.definitionFit: A calypso is a Caribbean style of song, originally from Trinidad.

clue.text: Twelve new rings Andy distributed

indicators.note: things distributed are scattered around, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: two rings, each shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Andy hands out twelve new rings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twelve' reads as a number of rings but means midday.
explanation.definitionFit: Noonday is midday, twelve o'clock in the daytime.
